pick.reason: The single amber square in a grid of dark cells makes "real pixels" visible. It reads in two seconds, gives each ratio a shape, and is the only rough that could only be Desk Studio's.
pick.lost: 2 spends the accent on a whole field instead of on one thing, sets the mark on amber, and leaves a dead black void under the headline. 3 is clean but generic: the accent on one word is the template move, and the portrait version has leftover air between the supporting line and the mark.
notes: Linkedin headline from about 76px to 95px (brand scale), line height 1.0, tracking -0.02em, still two lines ("Checked on / real pixels.") in the left column. At thumbnail size the headline should carry the left half, not sit in it.
Linkedin supporting line to 25px on one line, with no orphaned "round." Let it use the full left column (48px to 612px). A one-word last line breaks the block's shape.
Ig-post supporting line to 39px. Its current size of about 36px is off the brand scale (proof accepts only 16/20/25/31/39/49/61/76/95/119…).
Mark "deskstudio.ai" to 25px at both sizes, keeping #8a8a93. The standard says nothing readable goes under 24px, and the mark is readable.

Linkedin: align the grid's top edge to the headline cap height and its bottom edge to the mark's baseline, so both columns share the same top and bottom lines. Ig-post: put the mark baseline exactly at y=1215, on the 10% bottom safe line.

spacing: On linkedin, open the gap between the headline's last baseline (y≈235) and the supporting line's cap height from about 24px to 40px, moving the supporting line down 16px. On ig-post, move the mark baseline from about y=1207 to exactly y=1215, as in Art Director note 5.

composition: Make every grid cell square. On linkedin, use 54x54 cells with 8px gaps, 6 columns by 8 rows, spanning y=72 to y=560, with the mark baseline also at y=560. On ig-post, use 110x110 cells with 8px gaps, 8 columns by 6 rows, moving the grid top from y=504 to y=456 so it ends at y=1156, above the mark.

originality: The cells now read as 59x53 (linkedin) and 110x100 (ig-post) tiles. The "real pixels" idea depends on the amber cell being a true square pixel, so lock the amber cell to the same square size as its neighbours at both sizes. Keep its position: linkedin column 3, row 4; ig-post column 5, row 3.
polish: Use the same grid treatment on both sizes: linkedin has #0b0b0c cells on a #141416 panel, while ig-post has #141416 cells on #0b0b0c. Pick #141416 cells on #0b0b0c for both.
